correct_recommendations: In change_password, delete every refresh_tokens row of the user before it issues the new tokens for the current device. Other devices fail their next refresh, and their access tokens expire within 15 minutes.
invalid_options: Rotate SIGNING_KEY on a password change, because it logs out every user.
Shorten REFRESH_TTL, because other devices stay logged in until their refresh token expires.
Shorten ACCESS_TTL only, because the refresh tokens keep working.
Delete every session of the user including the current device, because the requirement keeps that device logged in.
root_cause: change_password updates the password hash and issues new tokens, but it leaves the user's other rows in refresh_tokens in place. Those refresh tokens stay valid for up to 30 days, so other devices keep getting new 15-minute access tokens.

dependent_facts.true_value: access token JWT 15 minutes; refresh token 30 days, stored hashed in refresh_tokens
change_password updates password_hash and issues new tokens; it does not touch refresh_tokens
the middleware checks signature and expiry only, with no database or Redis read
other sessions end within 15 minutes of a password change; the current device stays logged in
about 2,500 requests per second at peak; Redis quayside-cache is available
one HS256 key for all users; a rotation logs out every user

required_questions.question: Why do other devices stay logged in?
required_questions.expected_answer: Their refresh tokens stay valid for up to 30 days, and each refresh issues a new access token.

required_questions.question: Does the fix meet the 15-minute requirement?
required_questions.expected_answer: Yes. Other devices keep their current access token for at most 15 minutes and then fail to refresh.

required_questions.question: Does the device that changed the password stay logged in?
required_questions.expected_answer: Yes. change_password issues new tokens for it after the delete.

valid_alternatives.option: Per-request revocation check: store a token version or password_changed_at per user, put it in the access token, and check it in the middleware through Redis
valid_alternatives.trade_off: Ends other sessions at once instead of within 15 minutes, but adds a Redis read to every request at about 2,500 per second and a new failure mode when Redis is down.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The requirement tightens to immediate logout.

closing_decision: One decision: approve the refresh token deletion in change_password, choose the per-request revocation check, or a single follow-up on the chosen fix.

understanding.problem: A password change leaves the other refresh tokens of the user valid.
understanding.breaks: Other devices, for example a stolen phone, stay logged in for up to 30 days.
understanding.fix: Delete the other refresh tokens of the user in change_password.
understanding.cost: One DELETE statement in change_password; other devices keep access for up to 15 minutes.
